title: Physical vs chemical changes
keyIdea: A physical change makes no new substance and is usually reversible; a chemical change makes new substances. Mass is conserved in both.

kid: In a physical change, the stuff stays the same. Melted ice is still water. You can usually change it back.
In a chemical change, new substances are made. Burning wood makes ash, smoke and gases. Signs include a new colour, fizzing, light or heat. In both kinds of change, the total mass stays the same.
adult: Physical changes alter state, shape or mixing, but the particles themselves are unchanged, so they are usually reversible: melting, dissolving, evaporating.

Chemical changes rearrange atoms into new substances and are usually hard to reverse. Mass is conserved in both. If a gas escapes from an open container, the mass seems to drop, but the gas still has mass.

familyTip: Cook together and name each change: butter melting (physical), toast browning (chemical), sugar dissolving in tea (physical).

practice.explain: Browning makes new substances; the others are physical changes.

practice.prompt: {a} g of salt dissolves in {b} g of water. What is the mass of the solution, in grams?
practice.hint: Dissolving is physical: nothing is lost.

practice.prompt: {a} g of ice melts. What is the mass of the water, in grams?
practice.explain: Melting is a physical change, so the water still weighs {a} g.

practice.prompt: Which is a sign of a chemical change?
choices: A gas is given off and a new colour appears
practice.hint: Look for signs of a new substance.
practice.explain: Fizzing and a new colour show a new substance has formed.

pool.explain: Steam is still water, so it is a physical change.
New substances form in the egg, and it can't be undone.

pool.prompt: {a} g of magnesium burns in a closed jar and uses {b} g of oxygen. What mass of magnesium oxide forms, in grams?
pool.hint: Mass is conserved in a closed jar.

pool.prompt: {a} g of sugar dissolves in {b} g of tea. What does the sweet tea weigh, in grams?
Why is dissolving salt a physical change?
choices: The salt is still there: evaporate the water and it comes back
pool.hint: Can you get the salt back?
pool.explain: Evaporating the water gets the salt back, so no new substance formed.

pool.prompt: When wood burns in an open fire, the ash weighs less than the wood. Why?
pool.hint: Where did the missing mass go?
pool.explain: Carbon dioxide and water vapour went into the air; the mass still exists.

pool.prompt: Which change makes a new substance?
pool.hint: Changes of state don't make new substances.
pool.explain: Rust is a new substance, iron oxide.

visual.caption: Sort each change: is a new substance made? Drag a card, or tap it and then tap a box.
